one_month_reasoning: No SNOW earnings fall between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-30: Q3 FY27 (quarter ends Oct 31) is expected early December, date not yet announced (Q3 FY26 was reported 2025-12-03). In-window items: (1) the upsized $3.75B 0% convertible priced Sep 28 closes Oct 1; the convert-arb short-hedging pressure and the $548.3M repurchase of 2027 notes (with hedge unwinds) were executed around pricing, and the stock has already recovered from $328.1 (Sep 28 reference close) to $337.5, so I expect no further directional effect; the ~$3.7B of fresh cash opens the door to buybacks or M&A but nothing is announced. (2) Litigation: the company's motion to dismiss in the newer consolidated securities class action is due Oct 13 (a filing, not a ruling), and a ruling on the MTD in the older 10(b) action could land any time; either is a small valuation item and at most a one-day move. (3) Late-October hyperscaler results and the Oct 28 FOMC (hike odds fell to ~36% after the cool Sep 30 PCE print, per the supervisor's fact-check) can move long-duration software but give no directional edge. Post-earnings drift from the Sep 2 print has played out (spike to $384.56, then a $304-349 range). So I stay near-symmetric around spot: median ~$338, monthly sigma ~16% (slightly below 62%/3.5 = 17.7% because realized vol is inflated by two earnings gaps and there is no print in the window).

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM sales (12.5x ~$9.6B NTM revenue at Sep-2027 -> $314), NTM non-GAAP P/E (80x ~$4.05 -> $324) and adjusted FCF yield (50x ~$2.4B -> $314), each on ~388M diluted shares with ~$2.0B Sep-2027 net cash after the Sep-28 $3.75B convert; weights 0.4/0.3/0.3 give ~$317 twelve months out.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM (Oct-27 to Sep-28) total revenue ~$9.6B x 12.5x EV/NTM sales = $120B EV, + ~$2.0B Sep-2027 net cash = $122B equity / 388M diluted shares = ~$314

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $6.32B; product revenue is ~96% of total (Q2: $1.49B of $1.55B), so $6.07B/0.96 ~ $6.33-6.35B.

Exit growth 37-38% in Q3 guide, NRR 126%, RPO +30% and management's 'observed behavior' guidance (no change in methodology) support ~30% for FY28 with normal deceleration to ~25% in FY29; this lands product revenue near ~$9.9B in FY29, i.e. at/above the long-standing $10B FY29 product-revenue target reiterated at the June 2026 investor day.
~1/3 weight FY28 run-rate exit quarter plus ~2/3 FY29 first three quarters on the estimates above.

Today ~$128B diluted market cap less ~$1.3B pro forma net cash ~ $127B EV on ~$7.6B NTM revenue ~ 16.5-17x for ~35% growth. With growth fading toward mid/high-20s by late 2027 I compress roughly in proportion to growth (~0.5x per point). I stay at 12.5x rather than the supervisor's 13x centre because Databricks (company-reported >$7B run-rate, >80% y/y) is now larger than Snowflake and growing >2x faster, which argues against the top half of the 12-14x band.

Stock trades at ~152x FY27 consensus EPS ($337.5/$2.22) and ~100x my FY28; with EPS growing ~35-40% I use a PEG of ~2 on forward growth, i.e. ~80x, a multiple consistent with where high-growth infra software traded during 2026 (SNOW itself was ~65x forward at the April low of $118 on then-lower estimates).

Today ~$127B EV / ~$1.75B NTM adj. FCF ~ 72x. Adjusted FCF excludes GAAP SBC of ~27% of revenue (not 29%, which included payroll tax), so owner FCF is far lower; I haircut the multiple as growth slows toward 25%; 50x is roughly 2x the FCF growth rate. The SBC correction is too small to change the multiple.

bear.story: AI-driven acceleration proves a one-to-two quarter pull-forward: consumption growth slips back to the high-20s by mid-2027, FY28 guide in Feb-2027 comes in ~24-25%, product gross margin keeps sliding below 74% on lower-margin AI inference (frontier-model costs, $390M AI-provider commitment), and software multiples re-rate as they did in Feb-Apr 2026 when the stock fell to $118. ~8-9x NTM sales. Databricks (>$7B run-rate, >80%) keeps taking the incremental AI/data-engineering workload, and net cash of only ~$1.3-2.0B after the convert offers little cushion.

base.story: Growth decelerates gracefully from 37% to ~28-30% through FY28 (consensus FY28 +28%), operating margin expands toward ~17-18%, GAAP profitability on track for Q4 FY28; multiple compresses from ~16.5-17x to ~12.5-13x NTM sales, estimate growth carries the price modestly above today; the fresh ~$3.7B of convert cash funds some buybacks that roughly offset SBC dilution.

bull.story: CoCo/CoWork and Cortex keep compounding (AI already ~half of the acceleration), growth holds in the mid-30s into FY28, product revenue tracks well ahead of the $10B FY29 target, margins expand despite AI mix; market pays ~16-17x NTM sales on ~$10B+. Stock reaches the $479-531 CEO-PSU tranche zone. At $500 the stock sits right at the new 2029 notes' $500.38 conversion price (well below the $820.30 cap), so dilution from the new notes is still minimal.

thesis_break_reason: Around $215 (-36%, ~9x NTM sales) the market would be pricing product growth back toward ~20-25%, NRR sliding toward ~115-120% or clear share loss to Databricks, not ordinary 60%-vol noise; triggers would be a guide-down at the Dec Q3 or Feb/Mar Q4 print, product growth under ~28%, or product gross margin breaking toward 70% on AI costs. Caveat: a macro software liquidation took the stock to $118 in April 2026 without a fundamental break, so confirm with the fundamentals before acting on price alone.

reasoning: Round 2. Primary documents still show a re-accelerating business: Q2 FY27 product revenue $1.49B +37% (third straight acceleration), Q3 guide +37-38%, FY27 guide $6.07B (+36%), non-GAAP op margin 14.5%, RPO $9.0B +30%, NRR 126%. The supervisor's fact-checks fixed three things I had wrong or missed, and I verified the main one: the $3.75B 0% convertible priced Sep 28 ($2.0B 2029 at $500.38, $1.75B 2031 at $483.98, capped calls $383.5M with an $820.30 cap, $548.3M spent to buy back only $261.8M face of the in-the-money 2027 notes, ~$3.70B net proceeds; company release and Yahoo copy). That takes pro forma net cash to ~$1.3B (from my ~$2.05B) and ~$2.0B by Sep-2027 (from ~$2.5B), because FCF is largely absorbed by RSU tax withholding and buybacks. I now count debt at face with only ~5M net excess convert shares (388M diluted), avoiding the double count. GAAP SBC is 27.3% of revenue, not 29%. There is a second securities matter (MTD due Oct 13; a pending ruling in the older action), small in value. Databricks at >$7B run-rate growing >80% is a real competitive datapoint; I use it to hold my EV/sales multiple at 12.5x rather than move to the supervisor's 13x. Net effect: the lower net cash (-$1.3/share) is offset by fewer shares and higher interest income, so fair value moves from $316 to ~$317, still ~6% below spot, while sell-side targets (~$414-435, mostly Buy) sit above. I keep the 12-month median ~$338 (small drift: below-spot fundamental value balanced by revision momentum and the analyst skew) and a lognormal sigma ~0.47 with a slightly fat left tail; I trimmed the upper strikes by ~0.5-1pt for the Databricks share-shift risk and the thinner net-cash cushion. The 1-month ladder stays near-symmetric: the convert closes Oct 1 with its hedging already in the price, and the litigation items are small. Research this round: 2 searches plus EDGAR index check (no 8-K for the convert yet filed as of Sep 24 index); the BusinessWire page was blocked, so terms come via the company newsroom/Yahoo copies. No option data used.
